Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 45, verse 1:

Naming of the surah

• It is called al-Jathiyah (the Kneeling), because it mentions the kneeling of creatures out of fear, on their knees, awaiting the reckoning on the Day of Resurrection.

From the objectives of the surah

• Establishing that Allah, the Exalted, alone deserves worship, through the proofs of His power and oneness in the creation of mankind, of the animals, and of the heavens and the earth, in the giving of life to the earth by sending down rain, and in the alternation of night and day. In this there is a reminder of Allah's great blessings upon creation, which call for thanking the Benefactor and affirming the oneness of the Creator.

• Strengthening and consoling the Messenger (ﷺ) by telling him that the situation of his call with his people is like the situation of Musa's call, which is not free from opponents; that this does not discredit it or the one who brought it; and that he should not care about the obstinate or their great numbers. Also, there is an allusion to the similarity between the state of those who neglected to reflect on the signs of Allah and opposed the Prophet (ﷺ), and the state of the Children of Israel in their disagreement about their Book after knowledge had come to them, so Allah gave their enemy power over them.

• Rebuking the Dahriyyah (materialists), who denied the existence of the Great Creator, denied resurrection after death, and claimed that time (al-dahr) is what destroys people, and that there is no gathering, no reckoning, and no recompense. It also describes some of the horrors of the Day of Recompense, and in it is a warning (tarhib) of the torment prepared therein for the disbelievers.

[At-Tafsir]

﴿Ḥā Mīm﴾ The discussion of the disjointed letters (al-huruf al-muqatta'ah) has already been given at the beginning of Surat al-Baqarah.
This Qur'an is sent down from Allah, the Almighty in His vengeance upon His enemies, the All-Wise in managing the affairs of His creation.

Indeed, in the seven heavens, and in the earth from which creation comes forth, and in what it contains of creatures varied in their kinds and types, there are surely signs and proofs for those who believe in them.

**Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 45, verse 4:**

And in your creation, O people, and in the creation of what is dispersed on the earth of living creatures that crawl upon it, are proofs and evidences for a people who are certain of God and His law.

In the alternation of night and day and their succession over you, and in what Allah sends down from the sky of rain, by which He revives the earth after its dryness so that it stirs with vegetation and crops, and in the turning of the winds for you from every direction and their turning for your benefit, are signs and proofs for a people who understand from Allah His proofs and signs.

These verses and proofs We recite to you, O Messenger, in truth. So in what statement after Allah, His signs, and His evidences that He alone is the true God, with no partner, will they believe, affirm, and act upon?
Destruction for every liar, sinner of many sins.

This is a commentary on Surah al-Jathiyah (45), verse 8. The passage is the tafsir text itself, so it is translated below.

He hears the verses of Allah's Book being recited to him, yet he persists in his disbelief, arrogantly puffed up within himself against submitting to Allah and His Messenger, as though he had not heard the verses of Allah that were recited to him. So give him glad tidings, O Messenger, of a painful and agonizing punishment in the Fire of Hell on the Day of Resurrection, [this] liar and sinner.

When he learns anything of Our verses, this sinful liar takes them in mockery and derision. For such people is a humiliating punishment that will disgrace them on the Day of Resurrection, as a recompense for their mocking of the Qur'an.

Ahead of these mockers of God's signs is Hell. Neither their wealth nor their children, which they earned, will avail them anything, nor will the gods they worshipped besides God. For them is a great and painful punishment.

This Qur'an that We have sent down to you, O Messenger, is guidance from misguidance and a proof of the truth. It guides whoever follows it and acts by it to a straight path. As for those who denied the signs in the Qur'an that point to the truth and did not believe in them, they will have a painful, agonizing punishment, one of the worst kinds of punishment, on the Day of Resurrection.

Allah, glorified and exalted, is He who subjected the sea for you, so that ships may sail upon it by His command, and so that you may seek of His bounty through various kinds of trade and gain, and perhaps you will be thankful to your Lord for His subjecting that to you, so that you worship Him alone and obey Him in what He commands you and forbids you.

Wa-sakhkhara lakum mā fi as-samawāti min shamsin wa-qamarin wa-nujūmin, wa-kulla mā fi al-arḍi min dābbatin wa-shajarin wa-sufunin wa-ghayri dhālika li-manāfi'ikum. Jamī'u hādhihi al-ni'ami minnatun min Allāhi waḥdahu an'ama bihā 'alaykum, wa-faḍlun minhu tafaḍḍala bihi, fa-iyyāhu fa-'budū, wa-lā taj'alū lahu sharīkan. Inna fīmā sakhkhara Allāhu lakum la-'alāmātin wa-dalālātin 'alā waḥdāniyyati Allāhi li-qawmin yatafakkarūna fī āyāti Allāhi wa-ḥujajihi wa-adillatihi, fa-ya'tabirūna bihā.

Translation:

﴿And He has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens, including the sun, the moon and the stars, and whatever is on the earth, including animals, trees, ships and other things, for your benefit.﴾ All these blessings are a favour from Allah alone, which He has bestowed upon you, and a bounty from Him which He has granted you. So worship Him alone, and do not associate any partner with Him. Indeed, in what Allah has subjected for you there are signs and proofs of the Oneness of Allah, for a people who reflect upon the signs, proofs and arguments of Allah, and thus take heed from them.

Say, O Messenger, to those who believe in Allah and follow His Messenger: forgive and overlook those who do not hope for the reward of Allah, nor fear His punishment, when they inflict harm and injury upon the believers; that Allah may recompense these polytheists for what they used to earn in this world of sins and of harming the believers.

Whoever does righteous deeds, from among the servants of Allah, by obeying Him, does so for the benefit of his own self; and whoever does evil in this world by disobeying Allah, bears the consequence upon his own self. Then, O people, you will all be returned to your Lord after your death, and He will reward the one who does good for his good deeds, and the one who does evil for his evil deeds.

**Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 45, verse 16:**

We gave the Children of Israel the Tawrah (Torah), the Injeel (Gospel), and wisdom, and the judgment according to what is in them. We made many of the prophets among their descendants from Ibrahim (peace be upon him). We provided for them with good things: sustenance, fruits, and foods. And We preferred them over the peoples of their time.

We gave the Children of Israel clear laws concerning what is lawful and unlawful, and proofs that distinguish truth from falsehood. They did not differ except after knowledge had come to them, and the proof had been established against them. What led them to this was the transgression of some of them against others, out of desire for status and leadership. Indeed your Lord, O Messenger, will judge between the people of the Children of Israel who differed, on the Day of Resurrection, concerning what they used to differ about in the worldly life. In this is a warning to this Ummah not to follow their path.

Then We placed you, O Messenger, upon a clear path concerning the affair of the religion. So follow the Shariah upon which We have placed you, and do not follow the desires of those ignorant of God's law, who do not know the truth. In the verse there is a great indication of the perfection and nobility of this religion, the obligation to submit to its judgment, and the impermissibility of inclining toward the desires of disbelievers and atheists.

Indeed, these polytheists who associate others with their Lord, who call you, O Messenger, to follow their desires, will avail you nothing against the punishment of God if you follow their desires. Indeed, the wrongdoers, who transgress the limits of God, from among the hypocrites, the Jews and others, are allies of one another against the believers in God and those who obey Him. And God is the Helper of the God-fearing, who fulfill their Lord's obligations and avoid His prohibitions.

This Qur'an that We have sent down to you, O Messenger, is a set of insights by which people see truth from falsehood and recognize the path of guidance, and it is a guidance and a mercy for a people who have certainty in its authenticity and that it is a revelation from Allah, the Almighty, the All-Wise.

Or do those who committed evil deeds think that We will treat them the same as those who believed in God, affirmed His messengers, did righteous deeds, and devoted their worship sincerely to Him alone, and that We will make their lives and their deaths equal to theirs? Evil is their judgment, that they equate the wicked with the righteous.

God created the heavens and the earth with truth, justice, and wisdom, and so that every soul may be recompensed in the Hereafter for what it has earned of good or evil, and they will not be wronged; they will receive the reward of their deeds.

Have you considered, O Messenger, the one who has taken his desire as his god, so that he follows whatever his desire inclines him to do, and whom Allah has led astray after the knowledge has reached him and the proof has been established against him? He does not listen to the admonitions of Allah nor take heed from them, and Allah has sealed his heart, so he does not understand anything with it, and has placed a covering over his sight, so he does not perceive with it the proofs of Allah. Who, then, can guide him to the right and the rectitude after Allah has led him astray? Will you not then take heed, O people, so that you may know that whoever Allah has done this to will never be guided, and will never find for himself a guiding protector? The verse is a foundation for warning against desire being the motive that drives believers to their deeds.

This is the commentary on Surah al-Jathiyah (45), verse 24, from the King Fahd Complex's al-Tafsir al-Muyassar:

"And these polytheists say: 'There is no life but our worldly life; we live and die, and nothing destroys us but the passing of nights and days and the length of time.' They say this in denial of resurrection after death, and in refusal to accept that there is a Lord who causes them to perish and destroys them. These polytheists have no knowledge of that; they only speak on the basis of conjecture, delusion and imagination."

And when Our clear verses are recited to these polytheists who deny the Resurrection, their only argument is their saying to the Messenger ﷺ: "Bring back to life our forefathers who have perished, you and the believers with you, if you are truthful in what you say."

Say, O Messenger, to these polytheists who deny the Resurrection: Allah, glorified and exalted is He, gives you life in this world for as long as He wills you to live, then He causes you to die in it, then He will gather you all, alive, on the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt. But most people do not know Allah's power to cause them to die and then to raise them on the Day of Resurrection.

To Allah, glorified is He, belongs dominion over the seven heavens and the earth, in creation, possession, and worship. On the day the Hour comes, when the dead are raised from their graves and called to account, the disbelievers who deny Allah and reject the clear signs and evident proofs that He sent down to His Messenger will be lost.

And you will see, O Messenger, on the Day the Hour is established, every community and every religion kneeling upon their knees. Every nation will be called to its record of deeds, and it will be said to them: "Today you will be recompensed for what you used to do, whether good or evil."
This is Our record, which speaks against you with all your deeds, without any addition or omission. Indeed, We had been commanding the angelic recorders to write down your deeds against you.

As for those who believed in Allah and His Messenger in this world, and carried out His commands and avoided His prohibitions, their Lord will admit them into His Garden by His mercy. That admission is the clear triumph, after which there is no other triumph.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 45, verse 31:

As for those who denied that Allah is the true God and disbelieved His messengers and did not act according to His law, it will be said to them, as rebuke and reproach: ﴿Were not My verses recited to you in the world, but you were arrogant and refused to listen to them and to believe in them, and you were a people committing sins, and you did not believe in reward or punishment?﴾

When it was said to you, "The promise of Allah to resurrect people from their graves is true, and the Hour is beyond doubt," you said, "We do not know what the Hour is. We expect it to occur only as a mere supposition, and we are not certain that the Hour is coming."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 45, verse 33:

The evil deeds that they had done in the world become apparent to those who used to deny the signs of God, and there befalls them the punishment of God, the recompense for what they used to mock.

It will be said to these disbelievers: "Today We will leave you in the torment of Hell, just as you neglected faith in your Lord and working for the meeting of this your Day. Your dwelling is the Fire of Hell, and you have no helpers who could save you from the punishment of Allah."

This is the punishment of Allah that has come upon you, because you took the signs of Allah and His proofs as a mockery and a plaything, and the adornment of the worldly life deceived you. So today they will not be brought out of the Fire, nor will they be returned to the world so that they may repent and do righteous deeds.

So to Allah, glorified and exalted, alone belongs all praise for His countless blessings upon His creation, the Lord of the heavens and the earth, their Creator and their Sustainer, the Lord of all creatures.

And to Him alone belong majesty, glory, greatness, dominion, power and perfection in the heavens and the earth. He is the Almighty, who cannot be overcome, the All-Wise in His words, His actions, His decree and His legislation. Exalted and sanctified is He; there is no god but Him.
